JAK1 variant clustering — exploratory analysis

All 21,926 substitutions from jak1_clustering_rebuilt.csv · paper's Dataset EV1 clustering vs the rebuild · gnomAD r4 · generated 3 November 2026

Two clusterings of the same 21,926 JAK1 missense substitutions — the one published in Dataset EV1 and the one rebuilt here — agree on 84.9% of variants, ARI 0.484. This report asks what the features look like, how well each separates the clusters, where the two disagree, and whether either agrees with population genetics.

Cluster identity. Nothing in Dataset EV1 states which label means what. From the data it is unambiguous: cluster 1 = tolerant (AlphaMissense median 0.166), cluster 2 = damaging (median 0.953). All of this report uses that convention.

1. Feature distributions

Eleven features, each shown separately for the paper's two clusters. Coverage is in the panel title: five features are complete, three sit at 31.3% because dbNSFP indexes only single-nucleotide changes, and FoldX is at 94.9%.

AlphaMissense, PolyPhen-2 and ClinPred are strongly bimodal and separate the clusters almost completely. The two state-specific ΔΔG features are shifted but heavily overlapping, and ddg_delta is all but identical between clusters.

Sign convention, easy to get wrong. The Rosetta columns are ΔΔG = ΔGWT − ΔGmut, so negative = destabilising — the opposite of FoldX in the same table, where positive = destabilising (build_rosetta_ddg_jak1_info.md §2). Everything in this report is oriented so that larger always means more damaging. Scored with the wrong sign, ΔΔG closed appears to have AUC 0.26; oriented correctly it is 0.74.

2. Feature correlation

Spearman ρ on pairwise-complete observations, every feature oriented so that larger means more damaging, so all genuine agreement appears positive.

BLOSUM62 is the outlier — it is the only position-blind feature, a 20×20 lookup, so every V→F scores the same wherever it sits. The ΔΔG features correlate strongly with each other and weakly with everything else, which is expected: they measure thermodynamic stability, while the rest measure evolutionary or clinical pathogenicity. These are different quantities.

3. How well does each feature separate the clusters?

AUC for discriminating cluster 2 (damaging), computed on each feature's own coverage — so the rows are not directly comparable, since ClinPred, CADD and SIFT are scored on 6,873 variants and the rest on 21,926. The next subsection fixes that. The “vs rebuilt” column is self-referential — these features built that clustering, so it describes rather than validates. The fourth column asks a different question: can the feature tell a variant that is observed in gnomAD from one that is not? That is an external check, since no clustering used gnomAD.

Read the first column carefully. AUC is computed on each feature's own non-missing rows, so "own coverage" is not 21,926 for every feature — it is 6,873 for ClinPred, CADD and SIFT and 20,805 for FoldX. The n= under each value is what was actually used. That silent mismatch is precisely why the matched columns are needed: only there is every feature scored on identical variants.

On equal footing, AlphaMissense is the best feature — 0.9470 against ClinPred's 0.9463 — and PolyPhen-2 (0.9423) overtakes CADD (0.9284). The apparent lead of ClinPred and CADD in the previous table is an artefact of which variants they are scored on, not of how well they score them.

The dbNSFP subset is intrinsically easier. Every feature with full coverage gains on it: AlphaMissense +0.061, PolyPhen-2 +0.058, BLOSUM62 +0.022, FoldX +0.018. Single-nucleotide-reachable substitutions are the milder, better-characterised ones, so a clustering evaluated only there looks better than it is.

ESM-1b is the most robust. It is the only strong feature that barely moves between the two halves (0.8964 → 0.8884) and it is the best feature on the harder half, ahead of AlphaMissense (0.8551) and PolyPhen-2 (0.8515). Where the genomic predictors cannot go at all, the protein language model still works — which is the argument for weighting it more heavily than its all-variant AUC suggests.

4. gnomAD enrichment — the external validation

gnomAD r4 holds 934 missense variants for JAK1, 934 of which match a substitution in this dataset. Neither clustering used gnomAD, so the extent to which observed human variation avoids the damaging cluster is an independent test of both.

Both clusterings pass, and they pass equally. The paper's damaging cluster is depleted of gnomAD-observed variants (7.29% vs 2.67%, Fisher p = 5.6e-55); the rebuild gives 6.96% vs 2.58% (p = 4.0e-53). Purifying selection is recovered by an unsupervised split that never saw population data, and the two clusterings are indistinguishable on this criterion despite disagreeing on one variant in seven — so ARI 0.484 does not mean one is right and the other wrong.

The pooled figure is confounded — use the stratified one

100.0% of gnomAD-matched variants fall in the dbNSFP-defined subset, which is only 31.3% of all variants. That is structural rather than coincidental: gnomAD holds observed SNVs and dbNSFP indexes exactly the single-nucleotide-reachable substitutions, so the two sets nearly coincide. And the tolerant cluster is disproportionately inside it — 37.3% of C1 against 28.2% of C2. Pooling across the two strata therefore inflates the association: a textbook Simpson's paradox.

Clusteringpooled OR Mantel–Haenszel ORwithin dbNSFP, p
Paper (EV1)2.87 2.32 2.1e-32
Rebuilt2.83 2.4 1.1e-34

The finding survives the correction. Within the dbNSFP stratum alone the depletion is OR 2.32 at p = 2.1e-32, and the two clusterings stay indistinguishable (2.32 vs 2.4). The honest headline is the stratified odds ratio, not the pooled one. The second stratum carries only 0 gnomAD hits among 15,053 variants, so its apparent reversal is noise.

The gradient runs the right way: the commoner a variant is in the population, the less often either clustering calls it damaging. Variants absent from gnomAD are called damaging most often of all — as they should be, since they include everything purifying selection has removed.

Along the protein

The two curves run opposite: Spearman ρ = -0.546 (p = 7.2e-05, 47 windows). The JH1 kinase domain is the most damaging-dense and the most gnomAD-depleted region of the protein; the FERM–SH2 linker region is the most tolerant.

Within every band, coverage still costs 6.8 to 16.1 percentage points. The band effect is 3.0×, the coverage effect 2.1×, and they multiply — a 30-fold spread from the best cell (confident damaging at high coverage, 1.2%) to the worst (intermediate-low at low coverage, 36.5%).

6. What this does to the headline ARI

Subsetn AgreementARI
ALL — published headline21,92684.9%0.484
high coverage (≥10 of 11)6,87391.2%0.679
confident AlphaMissense15,00890.6%0.657
both4,93194.3%0.786
neither4,97668.0%0.130
The reproduction is better than ARI 0.484 suggests — but by less than the table implies. The bottom two rows stratify partly on AlphaMissense, which is itself a clustering feature, so 0.786 is a circular upper bound. The defensible figures use variables outside the feature set: ARI 0.679 at ≥10 features (coverage is fixed by codon reachability, not by any score) and 0.639 for variants observed in gnomAD. The headline is dragged down by 4,976 variants with sparse features and an intermediate score, which disagree 68% of the time at ARI 0.130, barely above the 53.6% permutation null. Those are substitutions needing two or three nucleotide changes, so CADD, SIFT and ClinPred are absent by construction, leaving Gower distance over 7–8 dimensions on a variant that is ambiguous anyway. Neither label is trustworthy there.
Why 0.786 is not the number to quote. The “confident” subset was defined using AlphaMissense, which is itself one of the eleven clustering features — selecting variants where a strong feature is decisive naturally selects variants both clusterings agree on. Stratifying instead on variables external to the feature set gives a smaller but trustworthy effect: ARI 0.639 for variants observed in gnomAD (n = 939) against 0.476 for those absent, and 0.679 at high coverage against 0.402 at low. Coverage is determined by codon reachability rather than by any feature's value, so it is not circular; the AlphaMissense split is. The direction of the conclusion holds either way, but the magnitude is 0.64–0.68, not 0.79.

This reorders the candidate explanations for the gap. Dropping all three ΔΔG features moves ARI 0.484 → 0.492; the HumDiv/HumVar choice is worth about ΔARI 0.090. Stratifying by data quality moves it 0.484 → 0.679 on the non-circular coverage split — still several times more explanatory power than either. The dominant cause is missingness interacting with the Gower distance, not a methodological difference between the two pipelines.

7. What follows

  • Both clusterings are externally valid and equally so. Stratified odds ratio 2.32 (paper) and 2.4 (rebuilt) for gnomAD depletion of the damaging cluster, p ≈ 10−33 within the informative stratum, from a split that never saw population data. The pooled figures (2.87 / 2.83) are inflated by the dbNSFP confound and should not be quoted.
  • The published assignment carries very different per-variant confidence, and EV1 does not mark which. On the non-circular coverage split, agreement is ARI 0.679 at ≥10 features against 0.402 at ≤8; on the fully external gnomAD split, 0.639 against 0.476. A confidence field — feature count plus distance to the decision boundary — would be more useful than further tuning of the clustering.
  • The ΔΔG features discriminate, but do not help. Oriented correctly, ΔΔG closed and open reach AUC 0.74 — on a par with FoldX at 0.72 — so they are not uninformative. Yet dropping all three improves agreement with the paper (ARI 0.484 → 0.492), which says they are largely redundant with FoldX while adding their own noise. ddg_delta is the genuine null at AUC 0.497.
  • Coverage is the lever worth pulling. The three 31.3% features are missing precisely where the clustering is least certain. Running SIFT and CADD natively, as PolyPhen-2 already was, would close most of the ill-determined set.

Open items

Two things this report flags but does not resolve. Both could change a number that is currently quoted, so they are listed as work outstanding rather than as caveats to be noted and forgotten.

ItemWhy it mattersWhat would settle it
gnomAD depletion is not mutability-controlled CpG dinucleotides mutate roughly 10× faster than other sites. If the tolerant cluster is enriched for CpG positions, part of the stratified OR of 2.32 is mutational opportunity rather than purifying selection. This is the one remaining route by which the headline could be materially wrong. Compute a trinucleotide-context mutability expectation per variant and test observed against expected, rather than observed against the other cluster.
gnomAD annotation gap at positions 665–708 45 records were excluded because their wild-type residue disagrees with P23458 under any constant offset. The window sits inside the JH2 pseudokinase domain — the region this project cares about most, and the one containing the V658F-equivalent position — so the gap is not in neutral territory. Identify which transcript gnomAD annotates there, map those records onto the canonical isoform, and restore them.

Caveats

  • The EV1 labels are not ground truth — they are the paper's clustering output, so ARI measures agreement between two unsupervised partitions, not accuracy.
  • Equal feature weights throughout; the paper's weights are not published.

Methods

Source JAK1/clustering/jak1_clustering_rebuilt.csv (21,926 rows, 11 features, both cluster labels). gnomAD r4 missense variants fetched from the GraphQL API by gene symbol and matched on (position, alternate residue) with the wild-type residue verified against P23458; 984 raw records were retrieved, 45 excluded on wild-type mismatch, and 934 of the remaining 939 matched a substitution in the dataset. Enrichment is reported both pooled and stratified by dbNSFP reachability (Mantel–Haenszel). AUC computed as the rank-sum statistic on each feature's own coverage, with features oriented so larger = more damaging. Enrichment tested by Fisher's exact test. ARI is the standard adjusted Rand index. Scripts: fetch_gnomad.py, analyse.py, plots.py, plots2.py, build_html.py.
